To strictly control the solar cell photovoltaic performance under various environmental conditions (temperature and percent relative humidity), we have also built a humidity and temperature- Page 34 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology controlled oven, and we located it in MIT.nano, MIT’s central shared facility that is accessible to any trained user. The environmentally-controlled oven is sufficiently sized to accommodate the Keithley 2400/LabView maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking system, or it can fit an LED chip on board that can simulate a solar-like spectrum. The view of the oven system is shown in Fig. 6.2 below. The system consists of three parts: a temperature-monitored oven system, a water tank attached humidity control system, and a wired port that enables us to connect instruments on the outside of the oven with the measurement unit and the light source positioned within the oven. Electrical testing is additionally done with multiple source measurement units (uSMU) that acquire current-voltage (JV) scans and maximum-power-point-tracking (MPPT) measurements under illumination. These measurements supplement the data from our self-built Keithley and LabVIEW MPP tracking system (Fig. 6.3a). We acquired 15 credit card-sized SMU boards for MPPT of multiple devices under illumination (Fig. 6.3b). Their lower sourcing voltages and currents (±5V, ±50mA) make them an affordable alternative to commercial SMUs from Keithley or similar manufacturers. The overall cost was ~$100 per board, significantly more affordable than competing low-cost SMUs, which are $1000 or more. These open-source boards were developed by Joel Troughton (https://github.com/joeltroughton/uSMU) for laboratory-scale PV testing. The light source utilizes the Seoul Semiconductor Inc. S4SM-1566509736-0C500H3S- 00001 LED Chip-On-Board (COB) which has a good emission spectrum match to solar radiation in the visible spectrum (Fig. 6.4b). With focusing optics and LED drivers, we expect each light source to have a cost of less than $200, be capable of up to 1.5 AM1.5 suns of illumination and be easily packageable for use in the 85/85 chamber. For long-duration runs, we acquired a system from Fluxim, which can provide 24 measurement channels, hold up to 4 samples at a time and be able to test devices under various atmospheric conditions and at different temperatures.
